The Bright Side:
Public scrutiny demands that politicians answer for practical governance rather than relying on abstract rhetoric.

Confusing personal theological belief (Q1) with constitutional governing capacity (Q5), reducing policy to piety.

Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders listens as President Donald Trump speaks during an event about healthcare in the Oval Office of the White House, Friday Sept. 18, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

Comment

Add as Preferred Source

Sarah Huckabee Sanders, governor of Arkansas, is running for president in 2028. Those who run for president always write a book about their lives to acquaint the electorate with who they are. Her book cover says, “Our identity in Christ and Christ alone is the only firm foundation for our future.”

Think about that Sarah. If the government fails to allow religious freedom and throws evangelical pastors and parishioners into concentration camps, Jesus doesn’t care? He just wants everyone to focus on him and certainly not on government constitutional freedoms, right?

Don’t you think there is maybe a teeny-weeny role for the secular world of government to play in religious salvation? God made the earth and everything in and on it, according to Genesis. But you’re telling me that God doesn’t care about the economy or about the government, only about living a good Christian life?

Jesus doesn’t need civil rights? He doesn’t need education? He doesn’t need law enforcement? He doesn’t need elections? All Jesus needs is proper worship?

Kimball Shinkoskey, Woods Cross
